assessment.summary: A handsome, feature-broad React 19 + Tailwind Pokédex whose at-rest desktop surface is genuinely well-crafted — authored animation curves, a hand-built CSS pokeball, correct stat bars and radar, skeletons matching real card geometry, toasts and a working error/retry state — sitting on top of a live-API data layer and several load-bearing defects. Adjudicating the audit: I accept the shareable-urls downgrade (the params do round-trip, but useUrlState.ts:67 hands App.tsx:56-67 a new `update` every render against a setState that always allocates, an unconditional render loop; and shared /?gen= and /?types= links render nothing because hydration never triggers data acquisition) and the responsive downgrade (the header row at App.tsx:342 and the Team Lab toolbar at TeamLab.tsx:134 neither wrap nor scroll below ~400px, and the Team Lab overlay has no backdrop click and no reachable close button on a phone). On the axes I accept architecture 4 over 5 — there is no prebuild of any kind, two full detail requests per grid card whose payloads are then sliced to 8/12 moves, a per-batch list call whose results are discarded, a Workbox CacheFirst cache sized at 500 entries against ~2,068 URLs with eviction anti-correlated to the access pattern, and no image caching — and robustness 3.5 over 4, because the 4.5 anchor's two conditions are met exactly (filters halt loading via App.tsx:280; dual-type matchups are not merely incomplete but wrong) and the submission adds a generation filter that renders ~0, a whole-app ErrorBoundary crash reachable from the evolution strip (App.tsx:799 stub → getSprite's unguarded `p.sprites.other`), and no creditable deploy since the recorded live URL serves a different application. uxDesign lands at 5.5: polished at rest, wrong in motion (rowHeight 170 vs a 184–211px card), broken chrome on phones, and mouse-only.
strengths: Stat visualisation is best-in-class for this field: correct /255 normalisation, a correctly-ordered clamped radar, and authored overshoot easing.

Real visual craft that does not read as templated — consistent radii and tracking, a hand-built CSS pokeball, tabular numerals, a coherent dark palette, skeletons whose geometry matches the real cards.
Breadth of surfaces: Team Lab with multiple persisted teams, Showdown import/export, PNG card and team export, compare, caught/shiny collection tracking, favourites.
The type chart in lib/damage.ts is a complete and flawless 18x18 Gen 6+ table with a correct dual-type product including immunities.

Error-handling scaffolding is real: every fetch is try/catch-and-return-null, loadInitial surfaces a user-visible error with a working Retry, an ErrorBoundary wraps the app, and the unfiltered browse path genuinely converges to all 1025 species.
weaknesses: useUrlState's unmemoized `update` plus App's effect dependency on it forms a permanent render/replaceState loop that starves the deferred search.

Every filter (search, type, generation) disables both the infinite-scroll observer and the load-more button, freezing the dex at whatever subset happened to be loaded with no way out but clearing the filter.
ensureDataForGen loads only up to a generation's FIRST id, so the generation filter renders essentially nothing.

The defensive matchup panel and team coverage use the primary type only and print raw damage_relations, so they state falsehoods (Charizard 'weak to ground') while a correct dual-type calculator sits unused in the same repo.
The evolution chain is flattened depth-first into one linear strip, inventing evolutions for every branching family (Eevee, Wurmple, Tyrogue).

Clicking an unloaded stage in that strip hands openModal a two-field stub and getSprite dereferences `p.sprites.other` unguarded — a whole-app ErrorBoundary crash that React swallows, so smoke tests report zero exceptions.
Phone layout: the header and the Team Lab toolbar overflow and overlap below ~400px, and Team Lab has no backdrop dismiss and no on-screen close button there.

Live-API data strategy with no prebuild, no persistence, no name index, no concurrency cap or retry: ~2,068 requests and ~18MB gzip of JSON plus ~120MB of uncached artwork, most of it discarded on arrival.

Dead and rotting code: AppStateContext is mounted but never consumed while duplicating App's localStorage writers, analysis.ts:52-58 is a 4-type stub chart, damage.ts's crit/boost parameters are never passed, and App.tsx:615 ships `{modalShiny ? 'SHINY' : 'SHINY'}` as UI copy.
The recorded live deployment does not serve this source (the CI deploys to a Cloudflare Pages project name that another submission also claims), so deploy health cannot be credited.
assessment.standout: The stat visualisation pair — a correctly-normalised bar set and a correctly-ordered, clamped stat radar, both animated with hand-authored overshoot curves — is the most convincing piece of work in the submission and the one place where craft and correctness meet.

assessment.summary: A 1,374-line vanilla-JS Pokédex with a genuinely strong prebuild and a striking Pokédex-as-terminal identity, sitting on a shallow feature spread. build-data.mjs pools 25-way with 5-attempt backoff over every /pokemon, /pokemon-species, /evolution-chain, /type, /ability and /generation resource, resolves generation from the /generation endpoint rather than id ranges, and emits four wire-compacted JSON files; the runtime confirms it works — all 1025 species reachable by scrolling, zero console errors, no exceptions. The single app.js is deliberately ordered (constants → pure helpers → domain functions → one view per route → router → listeners) and the hardest piece of logic in the brief, dual-type defensive effectiveness, is exactly right: I ran defensiveEffectiveness verbatim against live relations and Magnezone→ground 4x, Skarmory→poison/ground 0x, Spiritomb's three immunities all come out canonical. Against that: seven of the thirty features are absent (team builder, damage calc, moves dex, minigame, command palette, export, and filter-state URLs are effectively missing), and the two adjudicated downgrades are real defects rather than depth complaints — the Move Pool panel reads version_group_details[last] (app.js:412) and therefore renders learnsets that match no shipped game (Pikachu: 7 level-up rows vs 20 in SV, levels mixed from blue-japan/LGPE/BDSP/SV, 60 moves dumped into a bogus 'Train' tab), and the keyboard layer ships three bindings with no modifier guard so Ctrl+R and Alt+Left both misfire. The architecture stops one step short of its own ambition: four monolithic files all fetched before first paint (including 196 KB of evolution data the browse view never reads), zero cache headers in wrangler.jsonc, sprites hotlinked off an unpinned raw.githubusercontent.com branch at max-age=300, full-res 130-145 KB artwork used as grid thumbnails, and one core detail surface still calling pokeapi.co live per view with no memoization — even though build-data.mjs:59 already held the move data it needs.
strengths: Dual-type defensive matchups are fully correct — app.js:51-64 multiplies across both types so 4x/¼x emerge and immunities annihilate weaknesses; verified against live relations for Gengar, Skarmory, Magnezone, Dragonite and Spiritomb.

Build pipeline is the best part of the submission: 25-way concurrency pool with 5-attempt exponential backoff that rethrows instead of silently dropping (build-data.mjs:7-31), limit=100000 list fetches, generation resolved from /generation so forms get the right gen, deterministic sort, and wire-compacted output (positional stat/EV arrays, {n,h} abilities, precomputed has_art/has_anim/cry booleans).

Real branching evolution trees — build-data.mjs:83 recurses evolves_to and app.js:217-222 walks it breadth-first, so Eevee's 8 branches, both Wurmple lines and all three Tyrogue branches render with conditions paired 1:1 to nodes.

Visual craft is excellent for 462 hand-written CSS lines: a CSS-only Pokéball boot spinner, mix-blend-mode scanlines, staggered LED blinkers, an inline SVG data-URI favicon, a three-font system, type-derived --accent tokens, 7 keyframes plus a correct double-rAF stat-bar animation (app.js:383-385), and prefers-reduced-motion honoured.

Well guarded on every route it owns: missing-id, missing-chain and missing-species fallbacks, unknown type slugs still render the matrix, MOVES[name]||{}, a try/catch around the move panel and around boot(), an onerror sprite fallback on all six img sites, and junk hashes falling through to the dex.
weaknesses: Move learnsets are misattributed for every Pokémon: app.js:412 treats version_group_details[last] as the newest game, but that tail is now blue-japan/champions — Pikachu's level-up tab shows 7 rows against SV's 20 with levels mixed across four games, and Bulbasaur (unaffected by the 'train' bucket) mixes Gen-1 blue-japan levels with SV levels into a list matching no shipped title.

Keyboard layer breaks browser-reserved chords: no ctrlKey/metaKey/altKey guard at app.js:616-629, so Ctrl+R/Cmd+R navigates to a random Pokémon before reloading and Alt+ArrowLeft cancels Back; '/' only works on 1 of 5 routes because app.js:618 optional-chains #search with no fallback.

Accessibility is the weak half of the UX: exactly one aria-label in 648 lines (app.js:126, static 'favorite'), zero <label> elements, placeholder-only search, 18 type chips conveying state by colour alone with no aria-pressed, no aria-live on the result count, a keyboard-unreachable compare picker, no :focus-visible anywhere plus two outline:none rules, and --ink-faint #5d5b53 at 2.87:1 on bg colouring nearly all secondary microcopy at sub-11px sizes.

No caching story at all: no _headers, no headers block in wrangler.jsonc, no content-hashed filenames, no Service Worker; all four data files revalidate every load, and imgUrl (app.js:26) feeds full-res 130-145 KB official artwork into grid cards served from an unpinned raw.githubusercontent.com branch at max-age=300.

Data strategy is monolithic and one surface is still live: all four files (~1.24 MB raw, including 196 KB evolution.json and 38 KB abilities.json the browse view never reads) are fetched before first paint (app.js:633-637), and every detail view re-fetches ~290 KB from pokeapi.co with no memoization or persistence.

codeQuality scores near zero on the axis's own named criteria: one type="module" file with zero import/export, 11 module-level mutable bindings, no JSDoc/@type anywhere across 1,374 LOC, `list.length = 0; list.push(...fresh)` mutating a closed-over array by reference (app.js:199), byte-identical getJSON duplicated between the two build scripts, DEX.filter(x => x.default) + findIndex duplicated at app.js:251-253 and 622-626, and no package.json/lockfile/tests/lint.

Two unguarded boot-window paths: app.js:605-608 binds the RANDOM handler at module load while DEX is still [], so a click (or 'R') during the ~1.2 MB boot fetch does DEX[0].id and throws; and the localStorage favourites JSON.parse at app.js:18 runs at module top level outside boot()'s try/catch, so a corrupt value strands the page on the boot spinner.

Browse loop loses its place: route() app.js:597 does an unconditional window.scrollTo(0,0) with no history.scrollRestoration and dexView() resets renderCount=0, so Back from a detail page destroys both scroll position and pagination — after browsing to #900 the entire lazy-load must be redone.

Lossy derived fields: evolution_details sliced to [0] (build-data.mjs:84) so Leafeon/Glaceon show location instead of stone and Tyrogue's three branches read an identical 'Lv 20'; pickFlavor keeps one untagged English entry (build-data.mjs:35-38); compare bars hardcode max=200 (app.js:561) so 255 HP ties with 200.
assessment.standout: The build pipeline plus the type engine: build-data.mjs pools 25-way with 5-attempt backoff over ~3,700 endpoints, derives generation from the /generation endpoint's species lists instead of guessing id ranges, and compacts the output onto the wire — and the defensiveEffectiveness function it feeds (app.js:51-64) is one of the few in the field that combines both defending types correctly, including 0x immunities cancelling 2x weaknesses, verified line-for-line against live PokéAPI relations.

assessment.summary: A tight, well-factored React 19 + Tailwind SPA (1,581 lines across 21 source files, 3 runtime deps) fronted by a genuinely good Cloudflare Worker proxy: worker/index.ts allow-lists 14 PokeAPI resources, uses the Cache API with ctx.waitUntil(cache.put(res.clone())) plus cf cacheTtl/cacheEverything, and stamps s-maxage=604800 — the edge tier is real and verified working. scripts/build-index.mjs prebuilds a load-bearing 1025-entry index (types, gen, six stats, BST, height/weight, validated internally correct for 1025/1025 rows) that runs browse, search, all 11 sorts, compare and the reverse-index grids with zero network. The hand-written 18x18 type chart is provably perfect — I diffed all 324 cells against the canonical gen-6+ table with 0 mismatches — and dual-type defensive products combine correctly including 0x annihilation. Against that, three things pulled grades down on adjudication: MovesTable.tsx:22 picks the default version group as versionGroups[length-1] over Set insertion order, which is not chronological, so on a live 20-species sample 0/20 opened the newest game and 8/20 opened on 'champions' with all four method tabs empty; AbilityDetailPage's holder grid maps through the base-species-only index and silently drops 17.9% of holder rows (measured live across all 373 abilities), leaving 28 ability pages showing '0 Pokémon'; and the declared polish is partly undelivered (the .skeleton shimmer, scale-in and the Clash Display font are defined and used zero times). Accessibility is essentially unbuilt — one aria-label in the whole app, zero focus-visible and zero prefers-reduced-motion. Six disputed feature grades were downgraded on verified evidence; the axes moved architecture 8->7.5, uxDesign 8->7, robustness 8->7.5.
strengths: worker/index.ts: allow-listed edge proxy with Cache API + waitUntil + correct res.clone() ordering and cf cacheTtl/cacheEverything — verified live (cf-cache-status HIT on repeat, 403 on non-allow-listed resources).

src/lib/typechart.ts: all 324 chart cells correct against the canonical table, and defensiveChart multiplies across both defending types so immunities and 0.25x/4x land exactly.

Small, disciplined dependency surface (react, react-dom, react-router-dom) with a tsc -b build gate and SPA not_found_handling.
weaknesses: MovesTable.tsx:22 defaults to versionGroups[length-1] assuming Set insertion order is chronological; measured live, 8/20 sampled species open the Moves card completely empty (version group 'champions', learn method 'train' is not in METHODS) and none open on the newest game — and the dropdown is that same arbitrary order reversed.
AbilityDetailPage.tsx:17-20 filters holders through the base-species-only BY_NAME map: 527/2938 holder rows dropped (17.9%), 193 pages undercount, 28 pages render '0 Pokémon with this ability'.

assessment.summary: A broad, genuinely well-layered vanilla-JS Pokedex on a competent Cloudflare Worker: 17 ESM modules with a declarative route table, a clean pub/sub store, an api layer with in-flight request dedupe, and a Worker that edge-caches PokeAPI for 24h and exposes a smart composite pokemon+species endpoint. The hard logic most entries get wrong is right here — dual-type defensive multipliers combining both types with real 0x immunities, a live 18x18 type chart, recursive branching evolution chains, correct Gen III+ stat formulas with a proper HP branch, and correct team defensive coverage. What undercuts it is a single self-inflicted contract bug plus systematic truncation. api.js:33 getPokemon() and api.js:37 getCompositePokemon() are byte-identical requests to pokemon/:id, which src/index.ts:132 answers with {pokemon, species}; I confirmed against the live deployment that /api/pokemon/25 returns exactly those two top-level keys. Every caller expecting a flat Pokemon throws on the first dereference and lands in a blanket catch that stores empty state, so all 18 type chips, all seven base-stat sorts, browse-card type badges and backgrounds, the favorites type filter, and the Pokemon-of-the-Day hero are permanently and silently wrong — which is why a smoke test reports zero console errors on a page whose filters cannot work. Layered on top: abilities.js:24 drops 214 of 373 abilities (57%, measured live), the moves dex enriches only 400 of 934, flavor entries are cut to the last 5 of ~28 with no expander, and the Forms tab is gated on pokemon.forms.length so no Mega or regional form is reachable. Nothing typed could have caught any of this: only 140 of ~4,300 lines are TypeScript and `npx tsc --noEmit` fails outright with TS2688.
strengths: Correct in the parts that are hard to get right: detail.js:819-839 and team.js:248-262 multiply damage_relations across BOTH types (verified against live data for Gengar, Charizard, Magnezone, Skarmory, Sableye — all canonical, including true 0x), types.js:21 builds a live 18x18 matrix rather than hardcoding it, and detail.js:426-437 implements the real Gen III+ stat formulas with a correctly special-cased HP branch across all 25 natures (all 25 validated against PokeAPI).

A thoughtful Worker for a live-data strategy: src/index.ts wraps every upstream call in caches.default at 24h AND emits Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 for a genuine second browser tier; compositePokemon() collapses pokemon+species into one client request under its own namespaced cache key; wrangler.jsonc run_worker_first: ['/api/*'] keeps static assets off the Worker.

Real modular structure with no god-functions: a 12-line matchRoute over a declarative routes table, one module per view, a cohesive store.js (private-ish fields, guarded localStorage, event bus) with zero rot, and api.js:7-27 layering an in-memory Map plus a `pending` promise map for actual in-flight dedupe.

Genuine breadth of working surfaces: six standalone dexes, a 60-tile sprite gallery including every generation's shiny variants, an interactive stat calculator, recursive evolution chains decoding 17 trigger kinds, team defensive coverage, compare, favorites, and full dual-theme tokens with an eight-keyframe animation vocabulary that is actually wired.
weaknesses: One alias bug kills five surfaces permanently and silently: getPokemon() and getCompositePokemon() request the same route, which returns {pokemon, species}, so every flat-Pokemon consumer throws into a blanket catch. All 18 type chips filter an empty map, all seven stat sorts are inert (and 'total' yields NaN), browse cards never render type badges or type-coloured backgrounds, the favorites type filter always returns nothing, and the Pokemon-of-the-Day hero erases itself.

Systematic silent truncation across the dexes: 214 of 373 abilities dropped by a `!name.includes('-')` filter (57%, measured live) so speed-boost and water-absorb do not exist in the app; 534 of 934 moves left unenriched so type/category filters and power/accuracy/PP sorts silently cover under half the corpus; items enriched to 400 of ~2180; flavor entries cut to 5 of ~28 with no expander; learnsets enriched to 100 unique moves.

An active performance hazard: pokedex.js:308 fires enrichCards over the full 1025-entry list with no concurrency cap and no loading indicator, each fanning out to two upstream PokeAPI subrequests, and applyFilters() waits for all of them — selecting a stat sort stampedes ~2050 upstream hits and then changes nothing. There is no batch/index endpoint, which is the root cause of the typeless browse cards rather than a separate bug.

Accessibility is near-absent: 3 aria-labels total, zero role/aria-live/tabindex, zero :focus-visible (the three :focus rules are border shifts that also set outline:none), no focus trap or restore in the modal or search overlay, no skip link, and no prefers-reduced-motion despite infinite float/shimmer/pulse animations. 20 Tab presses never place focus inside a browse card.

Typing is effectively unenforced and rot is heavy: only 140 of ~4300 lines are TS, `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` fails with TS2688 (@cloudflare/workers-types is not a devDependency), package.json scripts are just wrangler dev/deploy/tail with no typecheck, lint or test. I scripted the import graph: 24 unused imports across 8 of 17 modules, plus 15 exported-never-imported symbols, the 20-entry type-colour map duplicated three times (data.js:1, utils.js:109, utils.js:126), the picker modal near-verbatim in compare.js and team.js each with its own hand-rolled debounce, and 135 inline style attributes over a 2125-line token stylesheet.

Data-correctness bugs beyond the alias: evolution reads only details[0] so Leafeon loses its Leaf Stone route, compares d.gender to the string 'female' when PokeAPI returns an int (Froslass and Salazzle both label 'Male'), and double-fires on stone evolutions producing 'Use Water Stone, Use Water Stone'; the Forms tab is gated on pokemon.forms.length > 1 instead of species.varieties so no Mega/Gigantamax/regional form is reachable; the offensive panel uses Math.max/first-wins and reports Gengar as 0x vs Normal and Steel.

Light theme is half-broken on the flagship page: styles.css:873/883/891 hardcode rgba(255,255,255,0.6-0.85) on .detail-id/.detail-genus/.detail-flavor while the header gradient goes pastel, leaving the genus and Pokedex entry at roughly 1.3:1 contrast beside near-black name text.
assessment.standout: The Worker's composite endpoint (src/index.ts:47) is the best single idea in the submission and the source of its worst bug in the same stroke: it collapses pokemon+species into one client round-trip and caches the merged result under its own namespaced key https://composite.local/pokemon/:id so it cannot collide with the passthrough entry — a genuinely sharp piece of edge design. But it shadows the plain /api/pokemon/:id path with a differently-shaped payload, and the client half is untyped plain JS with two identically-bodied accessors for it, so nothing in the codebase encodes or enforces the contract. That one unrecorded shape change is what silently disables the type filter, every stat sort, card type theming, the favorites filter and the home-page hero.

assessment.summary: A genuinely well-engineered static Pokédex: scripts/build-data.mjs compiles the entire PokéAPI surface into public/data ahead of time with a sha1-keyed on-disk fetch cache, 16-way concurrency, retry/backoff and 404-tolerance, and src/lib/api.ts is the only fetch site in the app, hitting nothing but /data/*. The compact positional move encoding plus vgIndex/methodIndex interning is what makes complete per-version-group learnsets for every variety affordable in ~8 KB brotli per species. The load-bearing logic is provably correct rather than plausibly correct — all 324 cells of the type matrix match the canonical Gen 6+ chart, defenseProfile propagates 0× immunities through both defending types with one shared implementation feeding detail/compare/team/typechart, evoTree renders real multi-branch evolutions with ~30 synthesized condition kinds, and the live index has exactly 1025 species with per-generation counts matching the official 151/100/135/107/156/72/88/96/120 split. The runtime smoke test is clean and reaches 1025/1025. Where it lands short of the top is depth per feature rather than breadth: the audit pass held eleven grades that were awarded as best-in-class against the fixed anchors and most did not survive — the browse grid, name search, single-key sort, artwork, shiny, flavor entries, compare, team builder, command palette, theming and responsiveness are all correct, complete, competent implementations with no distinguishing capability, which is the 2 anchor. The team builder specifically misses three of the five elements the rubric's own anchor enumerates (named multi-team storage, Showdown import/export, damage preview). Two derived-data figures on the flagship detail page are also wrong: format.ts:3-9 heightStr rounds inches without a foot carry, so 166 of 1025 species render impossible imperial heights like Charmander's '1′12″', and format.ts:23 catchPercent reports rate/255 under a '(X% at full HP)' label where the real full-HP figure is rate/765.
strengths: Build pipeline: sha1-URL-keyed disk cache under .cache/pokeapi makes ~7,700 resource fetches resumable and re-runs free, with 4 attempts / 1-4-9s backoff, 30s AbortSignal.timeout, 404→null and a 16-way pool — real engineering, not a for-loop.

Data correctness verified from the deployed artifacts, not trusted: 1025 unique species, zero rows where bst ≠ sum(stats), exact official per-generation counts, and a true 18×18 matrix whose 324 cells diff clean against the canonical Gen 6+ chart including every Fairy/Steel/Dark quirk.

Complete per-variety data model — build-data.mjs:520-548 gives every form its own types, pastTypes, stats, abilities, dimensions, art, cry, held items and full learnset, and DetailPage re-drives nine panels off the selected chip.

Crash-path discipline: every URL id integer-validated before use, csv params read defensively, resolveSpeciesKey → explicit 'No such Pokémon' state, ErrorBoundary re-keyed per pathname, Sprite onError fallback, localStorage stores shape-validated with try/catch on read and write, and exactly two non-null assertions repo-wide (both unreachable-safe). tsc --noEmit passes under strict.

Keyboard and accessibility work that is real rather than decorative — roving-tabindex Arrow/Home/End over the type grid, arrow-key tablists, combobox/listbox contracts in three search surfaces, skip-link into a focusable <main>, aria-live readouts, and a prefers-reduced-motion reset.
The team recruit engine (TeamPage.tsx:151-179), which scores all 1025 index rows by coverage-gap gain and rejects candidates that stack an existing ×4 weakness.
weaknesses: Two wrong numbers on the most-visited page: heightStr's missing foot carry produces impossible imperial heights for 166 of 1025 species (Charmander '1′12″'), and catchPercent's rate/255 is presented as '% at full HP' where the correct value is rate/765 — Bulbasaur is overstated 3× as 17.6% vs 5.9%.

No HTTP caching story of its own: wrangler.jsonc is 8 lines with no _headers and no assets.headers, so even content-hashed /assets/*.js and deploy-immutable /data/*.json are served max-age=0, must-revalidate. No service worker despite shipping a manifest, and no prefetch of prev/next shards despite arrow-key species stepping being a headline feature.

Media is unowned — the build persists raw.githubusercontent.com URLs and PokeCard renders the 475px official-artwork PNG (mean ~132 KB) into a 96px box with no srcset and no thumbnail tier, even though the pipeline already wrote the small sprite URL into every shard.

Dead payload and copy-paste: home/homeShiny/spriteShiny/spriteBack and spriteHistory[].backShiny are written into all 1025 shards and read nowhere; artUrl's shiny parameter is never passed by any of its four call sites; and HomePage re-implements rankSearch's id and fuzzy branches inline instead of importing the library six other files use.
HomePage.tsx:105 skips sorting while a text query is active at the default sort, leaving the ↑/↓ direction button inert but still announcing a state change.

The build's sanity guard fires at build-data.mjs:639, after every writeFile — it exits nonzero but truncated shards are already on disk and a later `npm run build` would ship them; `npm run data` is also not in the deploy path.

Adapts to width only: no (hover: hover) / (pointer: coarse) queries anywhere, so the favorites star and card type accent are invisible on touch, and viewport-fit=cover ships with zero env(safe-area-inset-*).
No pre-paint theme script — data-theme is set by initTheme() after the CSS and font imports, so light-theme users get a dark first paint.
assessment.standout: The build pipeline's compact learnset encoding: build-data.mjs interns version groups and learn methods into indices and stores each move as a positional [vg, method, level] triple, which is why a single ~78 KB / 7.9 KB-brotli species shard can carry all 17 Pikachu varieties with complete per-version-group learnsets and 17 sprite eras — and why MovesPanel can offer a real version-group + method-tab learnset browser per form with zero runtime API calls.

assessment.summary: A well-architected, tightly-written 4.4k-line React/Vite app whose core domain logic is unusually correct — the 18×18 type chart is derived from the API's live damage_relations rather than hand-typed (build-data.mjs:41-58 → util.ts:35-45), defenseProfile multiplies across both defending types including true 0× immunities, statAtLevel gets the HP/non-HP split, the flooring order and the Shedinja base-1 guard right (util.ts:70-76), and Tools.tsx:61 is the genuine main-series damage expression with the correct floor chain and correct asymmetric crit stage handling. The build pipeline is the strongest part of the submission: lib.mjs gives a resumable disk cache with 404 negative caching and 6-attempt exponential backoff, and build-data.mjs prebuilds every one of the 1351 varieties into static shards with zero runtime API dependency and no cap, slice or id range anywhere. What holds it back is a single hook defect with outsized blast radius: useInfinite (hooks.ts:57-65) keys its IntersectionObserver effect on [total, step] and returns early on a null sentinel, so any page that calls it above a multi-source loading gate never attaches an observer. Dex.tsx:99, Items.tsx:36, TypeDetail.tsx:18 and Dexes.tsx:19 all do exactly that, and there is no pager fallback — the flagship /pokedex hands a user 60 of 1025 species with only the passive caption 'Showing 60 of 1,025…', which also silently kills the alternate-forms browse toggle (forms are ids 10001+ and sort last). Alongside that sit four never-settling promises for unresolvable slugs (PokemonDetail.tsx:25 et al) that render a permanent spinner instead of the Empty state defined one line above — reachable not only from a typo'd URL but from the app's own evolution links, which uniquely use a species slug (PokemonDetail.tsx:392) against a Pokémon-keyed index. Accessibility is not thin but absent: zero aria-*, role or tabIndex in the entire source, no focus trap or restore on either overlay, and Picker.tsx — the modal gating team building, comparison and the damage calculator — handles only Escape, leaving keyboard users unable to select anything.
strengths: Data strategy is the anchor: build-data.mjs:255-403 prebuilds all 1351 varieties into static shards (form-specific stats, types, sprites, matchups) with no cap or truncation, backed by a resumable cache with negative-caching and exponential backoff in lib.mjs — zero runtime PokéAPI dependency.

Domain math is verifiably correct where it usually is not: derived (never hardcoded) 18×18 type chart, dual-type defensive multiplication with real 0× immunities, correct HP-vs-other stat formula with the right flooring order and the Shedinja guard, and a real damage formula whose crit branch correctly ignores the attacker's negative and the defender's positive stat stages.

One computation, one renderer: util.ts buildChart/defenseProfile back the Pokémon page, the 18×18 matrix, the dual-type composer, Compare's per-member matrix, Team's tallies and MoveDetail's effectiveness grid, so the six surfaces cannot drift apart.

Evolution rendering is genuinely graph-shaped, not first-path-only — Eevee's 8 branches, Wurmple's 2 and Tyrogue's 3 all render, with 18 evolution conditions decoded including relative physical stats, known-move-type, party species and overworld rain.

A real hand-built design system in 340 lines of CSS: Space Grotesk/Inter/JetBrains Mono pairing, 21 type colours, a pure-CSS pokéball brand mark, type-tinted card gradients via color-mix, a blurred saturated sticky nav, and an SVG hexagon radar with grid rings and axis labels — nothing templated.
weaknesses: One hook defect breaks the app's primary job: useInfinite (hooks.ts:57-65) never attaches its observer on Dex, Items, TypeDetail or Dexes, and with no pager fallback the flagship browse page measurably stops at 60 of 1025 species.

Four detail routes return `new Promise<never>(() => {})` for an unresolvable slug, so useAsync never settles and the user gets a permanent spinner instead of the Empty state — reachable from the app's own evolution links, which are the only links in the codebase built from a species slug rather than an index name (~15 chains dead-end).

Accessibility is at zero: no aria-*, role or tabIndex anywhere, no dialog semantics/focus trap/focus restore on either overlay, .sr defined and never used, no prefers-reduced-motion or prefers-color-scheme, and a dark-hardcoded index.html that flashes for light-theme users.

Alternate-form labels prefer PokéAPI's form_names over names (build-data.mjs:262), so ~200 of 326 forms lose the species name entirely — /pokemon/rattata-alola renders

Alolan Form

— and every tool (Picker, Guess, Random, TypeDetail) filters isDefault, so Mega and regional forms cannot be teamed, compared or calculated with.

Shipped-but-unread and mislabeled data: move `machines` carry a resource `url` nothing ever resolves (so TM numbers show as version-group badges), the Moves tab defaults to the highest-order version group `champions` whose only method is `train`, and Tools.tsx:150 labels a max-damage figure 'Guaranteed KO in'.

assessment.standout: The build pipeline. scripts/lib.mjs + scripts/build-data.mjs fetch every species, pokemon, form, move, ability, item, type, berry, encounter table and evolution chain at ?limit=100000 behind a resumable on-disk cache with 404 negative caching and 6-attempt exponential backoff, then emit per-entity static shards plus a lean index — all 1351 varieties, no slice, no id range, no early break — so the entire app runs off static JSON on Cloudflare with zero runtime API dependency. The tragedy of the submission is that a four-line ordering mistake in a 10-line infinite-scroll hook prevents the user from ever seeing more than 60 of what that pipeline so carefully produced.

assessment.summary: An exceptionally well-engineered static Pokédex: ~32.7k lines across 146 TypeScript files with zero `any`, zero suppression comments and zero TODO markers, strict TS (plus noUnusedLocals/Parameters/verbatimModuleSyntax) gating the build, a pure-function domain layer (types, damage, stats, evolution, coverage, filtering) that never imports React, and a dependency-free build pipeline that resolves 638k learnset rows and 117k encounter rows into thousands of static shards with zero runtime API dependency. The core logic is reference-grade and independently verified: the type chart is the real veekun efficacy table (324 cells, 23 quirk assertions pass) with era-aware past overrides, the damage engine reproduces the cartridge's exact floor/pokeRound nesting and convolves the full 16-roll distribution for nHKO odds, the stat formulas handle both classic traps (Shedinja base-1 HP, nature applied after the floor), and evolution is a genuine recursive branching tree with cross-chain root resolution. Coverage is complete — 1025/1025 species reachable live with zero console errors. The adjudication sustained the auditor on all seven disputed features and both disputed axes, because the pattern is consistent: many surfaces are correct, complete, and exactly one step short of the top anchor (a tri-state type predicate with no counts or negation, a shiny flag threaded everywhere but with no shiny-specific surface and a toggle that does not reach the per-game tiles, per-Pokémon matchups that are defence-only and current-gen-only, favourites that cannot be starred from the browse grid, a keyboard layer that declares role="tablist" on 26 controls it never wires). Three findings are outright bugs rather than shallowness: alternate-form sprites are keyed off the wrong id space so non-default form rows silently render a different Pokémon; index-entry generation comes from the species row so generation filtering is wrong for all regional and Mega forms even though the builder reads the correct column elsewhere; and the landing page's primary search CTA throws an uncaught TypeError while 5 of the palette's 18 page results 404 against a stale hand-duplicated route table. Still the strongest submission in the field on engineering substance — the deductions are about the last mile, not the foundation.
strengths: Domain logic is reference-grade: exact cartridge damage nesting with pokeRound and full 16-roll KO-chance convolution, correct HP/stat formulas with the Shedinja and nature-order traps handled, an 18-modifier ability layer that re-types the defence profile, and the real Gen V catch formula.

Type effectiveness is derived from type_efficacy.csv rather than hand-written, verified complete (18×18, 324 cells) and correct on 23 quirk cases, with historically accurate past-override replay so a Gen I chart has no Fairy — and one shared implementation feeds all nine surfaces that need it.

Zero runtime data API: the only client fetch is /data/*, backed by a documented positional-tuple wire contract, an in-flight-deduping cache with typed DataError, lazyWithRetry guarding the stale-shell chunk-404 white screen, and verified production cache headers plus HTMLRewriter OG injection on the shell.

Typing and layering discipline: strict tsconfig gating the build, every specifier across 146 files resolving, src/lib never importing components/pages, builders importing only node:* plus the shared src/types/data.ts contract, 215 `///` doc comments and zero inline comments, and data-driven spec tables instead of switch ladders.

Deliberate error handling that survives abuse: /pokemon/notarealpokemon renders a real NOT FOUND panel, garbage filter query state parses through allow-lists to '1,025 matching' instead of emptying, and the dex provider has an explicit failure screen with retry.
weaknesses: Two wrong-data bugs visible in the live UI: builders/pokemon.ts:397 feeds a pokemon_forms.id into sprite paths keyed by pokemon.id (Unown-B renders deoxys-attack, and the fallback chain cannot fire because the wrong file exists at 200), and :296 takes generation from the species row so raichu-alola reports Generation I and the generation filter misfiles every regional/Mega form.

The landing page's primary control is dead and throws: home/commandPalette.ts forges a ⌘K KeyboardEvent on `window` while AppShell.tsx:30-36 evaluates target.closest(...) first, so the hero search button and the 404 page's only button both emit an uncaught TypeError.

Publicly reachable 500s in the worker: unguarded COLLECTIONS[segments[0]] prototype lookups (/api/constructor, /api/toString) and raw decodeURIComponent at :177 and :303 while safeDecode sits at :96 — /pokemon/%, a document route that should have served the SPA, hard-fails.

Bounded but genuine rot against the 9 codeQuality anchor: a hand-duplicated route table that has already drifted (5 dead entries), divergent duplicate helpers (two generationRoman with different sentinels, three formatPercent with incompatible contracts, five ROMAN tables, three clamp), ~9 dead exports, SPECIES_TOTAL hardcoded in two pages, and a 687-line DamageCalculator default export.

An ARIA contract announced and not implemented: ui/Controls.tsx Segmented declares role="tablist"/role="tab" in 26 places with no keyboard handling, and the mobile nav drawer lacks the Escape/trap/scroll-lock its own sibling FilterSheet implements.

Service-worker hygiene: public/sw.js pins VERSION='pokedex-v1' with no build stamping while serving /data/* cacheFirst with no revalidation, so the activate-time purge can never fire and an installed client can serve last-deploy JSON indefinitely.
assessment.standout: The domain layer: a React-free src/lib that reproduces the cartridge damage formula floor-for-floor with pokeRound at each documented step and convolves the full 16-roll distribution into exact nHKO probabilities, sitting next to a type engine derived from veekun's efficacy CSV with descending-order past-override replay so the 18×18 matrix is historically correct per generation — one shared implementation feeding the detail page, compare, team analysis, coverage and the calculator alike.

assessment.summary: A zero-dependency vanilla-JS Pokedex on Cloudflare Workers whose strength is its data pipeline: scripts/ingest.js pulls all 1025 species plus every referenced move, ability, item and type from PokeAPI with pooled concurrency, retries and resume-on-restart, transforms them into compact payloads and writes chunked bulk NDJSON that is loaded into KV; src/index.ts then serves nine JSON endpoints straight from KV with batched multi-key gets and s-maxage/stale-while-revalidate headers, so nothing hits PokeAPI at request time. The split is stark: the worker and the ingest script are production-shaped, while the 1105-line public/app.js carries the defects — a mis-wired reference that makes the Matchups tab render the literal word 'undefined' in all 36 rows for every species, offensive type effectiveness computed as a product of the attacker's own two types, a search that cannot find the hyphenated names it prints itself, and method chips that show a fraction of each learnset. It covers the core dex competently (full 1025 browse verified live, filters, an excellent stats tab, a recursive branching evolution tree, compare) and stops there: no team builder, damage calculator, standalone moves dex, type chart, minigame, command palette or export, and no alternate forms at all because ingest hard-filters to ids 1-1025.
strengths: Data architecture: a resume-safe pooled ingest (ingest.js:56 pool, ingest.js:94 skip-already-done, ingest.js:30 retry/backoff) feeding chunked bulk KV writes, with the worker doing batched multi-key KV reads (src/index.ts:40-56, capped at 64) behind real cache-control headers — the whole dataset is prebuilt and runtime has zero PokeAPI dependency.

The worker and its type model are the best-written code in the submission: strict-TS dispatch with typed KV reads, regex-bounded id validation, per-route 404s, a single try/catch 500, SPA fallback and `satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>` (src/index.ts), against a hand-written 128-line domain model (src/types.ts).

The stats tab matches the exceptional anchor: double-rAF animated per-stat bars with per-stat gradients plus a hand-built SVG radar (app.js:628) with rings, axis lines, polar maths, labels and a gradient fill, plus BST and average.

Evolution is genuinely branching and thoroughly labelled: parseNode recurses over evolves_to mapping every evolution_details entry (ingest.js:321), and parseTrigger hand-writes 13 trigger kinds including Legends-Arceus mechanics (agile/strong style, tower-of-darkness, three-critical-hits) with time-of-day, rain and location suffixes — Eevee renders all 8 branches with 6 distinct triggers on Leafeon.
weaknesses: The Matchups tab ships a mis-wired reference: tag is written as (m) => m.t but called as tag(t) with a string (app.js:848,851,853), and TYPE_ICON — a function — is indexed as an object, so all 36 rows render a grey badge reading 'undefined' with no type name. tsconfig.json scopes typecheck to src/** only, so the file containing the bug is never type-checked, and smoke.mjs screenshots the tab without asserting content.

Offensive type effectiveness is computed wrong: app.js:835 multiplies the Pokemon's own two types together against each defender, so Charizard is shown at 4x into grass and bug instead of two separate 2x STAB options. The defensive table (app.js:823) is correct, including 0x immunities.

Search cannot find the names the app itself renders — cards display 'ho oh' (app.js:272) while matchesSearch tests the raw 'ho-oh' (app.js:176), so all 76 hyphenated species return zero for their displayed name.

Learnset method chips are truncated by design: app.js:751 assigns each move a single bucket by priority, so on Charizard 88 of 131 multi-method moves are missing from every chip but their highest-priority one.
No alternate forms at all — ingest.js:88 filters to ids 1-1025, so mega/Gigantamax/regional varieties are never fetched.

Mobile browse is rough at the most common phone width: measured at 390x844 the grid collapses to one column while a never-collapsing sticky topbar plus 18 wrapped type chips and 3 selects eat ~40% of the viewport, and the sticky offsets are hardcoded 10px short (.filters-wrap top:55px against a 65px topbar, styles.css:142; .detail-tabs top:53px against a 65px head, styles.css:345), clipping the first chip row behind the bar on every screen.

Accessibility stops at the surface: the modal never moves focus in and has no focus trap, role=tab buttons carry no aria-selected/aria-controls, single-select type chips are role=checkbox, and the sprite-mode select's only label is an .sr-only class that is never defined in the stylesheet.

assessment.summary: LunaDex is a visually confident, strictly-typed React/Vite Pokédex fronted by a genuinely well-built Cloudflare Worker proxy — same-origin /api/pokeapi, method guards, Cache API keyed on the upstream URL so the cache is shared across users, ctx.waitUntil, s-maxage=86400, a logged 502 fallback, and identical path handling in dev/preview/prod. src/types.ts hand-models the PokéAPI surface with zero `any` under strict, layering is clean, and the deployed site is smoke-clean: no console errors, no exceptions, working detail route, real pagination to all 1025 species. The failure modes are all one level below the surface. The data strategy is the weakest link: no prebuild at all, a full ~270KB /pokemon/{id} document pulled per card to render four fields, an in-memory Map as the only detail cache, and a sidebar that advertises 'Offline mode · Cached notes available' when no service worker exists anywhere in the tree. Correctness has four confirmed defects — the Forms tab 404s on every non-default variety (verified live: pokemon-species/10033 returns 404 while pokemon/10033 returns 200), 326 indexed forms are counted in the hero but unreachable in every view, getGeneration's `?? "9"` fallback inflates the on-screen Paldea count, and the detail-hydration effects list detailMap in deps while always returning a fresh object, so a persistently failing fetch loops forever. On adjudication I rejected the audit's headline code-quality claim — the failing `tsc -b` is caused by a missing worker-configuration.d.ts, which the benchmark's own vendoring strips as generated output (`npm run cf:types` regenerates it), not by model error — but confirmed every other disputed point against the source, and moved architecture, UX and robustness down accordingly.
strengths: src/worker.ts is real edge craft, not boilerplate: OPTIONS/method guards, caches.default keyed on the upstream URL (shared across users), ctx.waitUntil(cache.put), max-age=3600 + s-maxage=86400, structured-log 502 fallback — and vite.config.ts mirrors the same path in dev and preview so one code path serves all three environments.

Strict, hand-modeled type layer: src/types.ts covers the PokéAPI surface with zero `any` under strict:true, every component has a props interface, and storage.ts:11 uses a real type predicate rather than a cast.

Hand-built design token system with complete light/dark overrides and color-scheme (styles.css:3-47), global :focus-visible outlines, skeleton loaders in both grid and drawer, an animated toast, and a drawer that becomes a bottom sheet on phones — the desktop experience is the strongest thing here.

Thorough null-guarding on optional PokéAPI fields — sprite chains with a URL fallback, types[0] guards, habitat/growth_rate/color/shape, cries, base_experience, findEnglish fallback, evolution_chain guarded even though the type says non-null — and no reachable uncaught exception in the shipped build.
Genuine pagination rather than truncation: the index is un-sliced and Load More adds 36 with no ceiling, so all 1025 species are reachable; the type atlas even honestly footnotes 'Showing 8 of N'.
weaknesses: The Forms tab fails on 100% of its links — species.varieties yields ids >=10001 for every non-default form and pokemon-species/{that id} is a live 404, so Promise.all in getPokemonProfile rejects and the whole drawer collapses to 'Field notes unavailable'; the URL is already rewritten to ?pokemon=10034, so reloading or sharing pins you to the error.

No mobile navigation at all: .primary-nav exists only inside .sidebar, which is display:none at <=720px, and the mobile topbar carries only brand/theme/search — Archive, Squad room and Type atlas are unreachable on a phone. The 'Open menu' button that looks like the fix has no onClick and is display:none in every viewport.

The advertised offline tier does not exist: index.html links a webmanifest and the sidebar prints 'Offline mode · Cached notes available' / 'Local cache only', but grep for serviceWorker across src/ and public/ returns nothing and only the name index is persisted — every card and drawer fails offline, and the detail-hydration effects then spin in an unbounded refetch loop because they return a fresh detailMap object on every round while listing detailMap in their deps.

Two wrong numbers on screen: the hero prints 1,351 'species indexed' while GENERATIONS caps every range at 1025, so 326 of those are unreachable; and getGeneration's `?? "9"` fallback buckets all of them into Gen IX, so the signal card shows 'Paldea · 446 entries' instead of 120. capture_rate (0-255) is also rendered with a '%' suffix.

No matchup logic anywhere — no product of multipliers, no 0x handling, no per-Pokémon weakness panel; the type atlas shows four of six damage_relations categories and omits the entire immunity column, and the team view labels a type census as 'Type coverage'.

Readability rot at scale: 22 JSX lines exceed 400 characters, peaking at 1432 (PokemonDetailDrawer.tsx:217) — the sidebar, header, filters panel, signal grid and team dashboard are each one unbroken line — inside a 366-line App.tsx god component with 16 useState, 10 useEffect, the 22-prop ExploreView call pasted verbatim twice, four dead exports, and a redundant 36-request burst on mount that duplicates the effect two blocks below it.

Accessibility stops at labels: aria-modal="true" with no focus trap, initial focus, focus restoration or scroll lock; no aria-current/aria-selected or tab roles; zero prefers-reduced-motion rules across 3,739 lines of CSS despite three infinite animations; a ⌘K chip bound to nothing.
assessment.standout: The Cloudflare Worker proxy — a correctly-implemented shared edge cache (cache key on the upstream URL, ctx.waitUntil, s-maxage, X-Pokedex-Cache HIT/MISS, structured-log 502) with the identical /api/pokeapi path mirrored through vite's dev and preview servers, so dev, preview and production run one code path.

assessment.summary: A well-organised, attractive React SPA on a Cloudflare Worker whose principal view is dead on arrival. Layering is clean (api.ts → useData.ts hooks → views/ui/components), the Worker's KV proxy is a genuinely good piece of work, and the browse grid is one of the better-looking ones in the field. But PokemonDetail.tsx:427 stores PokeAPI's `move_learn_method` — an object {name,url} — as if it were a string and :453 calls .replace on it, and with no error boundary anywhere in src/ the throw unmounts the entire app. Every species detail page is a white screen, which takes artwork variants, shiny, cries, the radar, stat bars, abilities, evolution, moves, matchups, flavour entries and the only way to add a favourite down with it. Behind that, the data logic that would have rendered is itself wrong in three independent ways: the type engine (useData.ts:68-105) files resistances in the `zero` bucket so 0.5x is reported as 0x and no 0.5 exists anywhere in the codebase; the matchup panel labels super-effective attackers as 'Strong Against' (PokemonDetail.tsx:294), inverting every defensive readout; and evolution chains are fetched by pokemon id instead of species.evolution_chain.url (useData.ts:44-45), so Pikachu's page would show the Growlithe line. The Worker fetches a correct, complete damage_relations table for all 18 types and then throws it away in favour of the broken local one (TypeChart.tsx:20 vs :94). Two secondary routes, #type and #compare, do render cleanly, and the browse page has a real working 'Load 120 more' pager that the smoke harness missed — which is why this is not lower. Adjudication: I accepted the audit on shareable-urls (0), flavor-entries (1), architecture (4.5) and robustness (2), all verified against the source; uxDesign lands at 4 rather than the audit's 3, because the surviving surfaces show real visual craft that the 'unstyled' anchor does not describe; and I extended the same runtime-crash finding to the detail-only features I had previously graded 2 (artwork, shiny, cries, stats-viz, favorites) plus national-dex and responsive, since grading flavor-entries down for the crash while leaving its neighbours at 2 would be incoherent. I also found, independently of both passes, that the generation dropdown's romanize() (Dex.tsx:116-128) indexes a 10-character string with a 13-entry table, so all nine options render as 'Gen undefined'/'Gen V'.
strengths: src/worker.ts:29-54 is a real edge-cache: KV get, upstream fetch, non-blocking waitUntil put behind a 6MB serialization guard, 24h TTL from an env var, x-cache header, CORS — and it verifiably HITs on repeat.

assessment.summary: A visually confident, data-complete Pokedex whose static index layer is the real achievement and whose detail layer is where it comes apart. scripts/generate-data.mjs is a properly engineered fetcher (backoff retry, 404 passthrough, 24-way pool) emitting seven key-minified indexes that I verified complete and correct end to end — 1,025 contiguous base species plus 326 forms, 937 moves, 373 abilities, 2,223 items, 68 berries, an exact 18-type chart — so browse, search, eight-key sort, type/gen/legendary/mythical faceting, the type matrix, team analysis and compare are all zero-network and all arithmetically right. Against that, the detail route re-fetches over the wire data the app already shipped (AbilityCard and MoveDetailModal both ignore the resident ABILITIES/MOVES indexes), fires GET /pokemon-species/0 on every load because `speciesId ?? 0` defeats its own null guard, and carries three stale-state defects from the same missing-reset discipline: the cry button keeps the previous species' Audio, the flavor-text index is never reset so the counter goes out of range, and the evolution view resolves nodes against a map keyed on Pokemon names rather than species names, giving ~21 species placeholder art and 404 links. The documented regeneration command crashes on four null-firmness berries before writing types.json and generations.json — both hard imports — so the pipeline that produced the app's defining asset cannot be re-run; the shipped data came from three undocumented patch scripts in an unrecorded order. Accessibility below the aria-label layer is unbuilt: no Escape, focus trap or role=dialog on any of four modals, no keyboard path to any move detail, no prefers-reduced-motion despite two infinite animations. Adjudicating the audit: I accepted every downgrade it argued (national-dex, artwork, moves-dex and theming are complete-and-correct 2s rather than best-in-class; cries, evolution and flavor-entries have confirmed wrong-output paths), extended the same evidence to forms, and rejected its robustness upgrade to 8 — its own findings elsewhere show three user-visible wrong-output defects, not four cosmetic ones.
strengths: The static index prebuild is real and verified complete at full scale — 1,351 dex entries, 937 moves, 373 abilities, 2,223 items, 68 berries, 9 generations — making every browse, filter, sort and analysis surface zero-network

Type effectiveness is exactly right: utils.ts:33-43 multiplies across all defending slots for true 4×/0.25×/0× results, off a types.json I checked row-by-row against the canonical Gen6+ chart, with one implementation shared by the detail grid, compare, team analysis and the 18×18 matrix

All 326 alternate forms ship as first-class browsable entries with working detail pages, and PokemonDetail.tsx:36 correctly resolves a form's species via species.url rather than naively reusing the form id

Motion is used with intent rather than decoration — capped index-staggered card entrance, a hero spring keyed on id+shiny so the shiny toggle re-animates, width-animated stat bars with per-stat delay, spring modals via AnimatePresence — plus skeletons at three granularities
Genuine responsive engineering: the moves table progressively drops columns and substitutes a mobile-only effect line, rather than just reflowing a grid

Layered, non-decorative error handling — query-error page on the detail route, artwork→sprite image fallback that demonstrably rescues form sprites PokeAPI lacks artwork for, try/caught localStorage reads, caught audio play() rejection, SPA _redirects for deep links
weaknesses: Three stale-state defects from the same missing-reset discipline, all reachable by ordinary detail→detail navigation to a cached target: the cry button plays the previous species' audio indefinitely, the flavor counter renders out-of-range values like '4/2', and neither has a key or reset effect

EvolutionView resolves nodes via DEX_BY_NAME.get(species.name) against a map keyed on Pokemon names — 21 of 22 sampled species miss, so Espurr→Meowstic, Frillish→Jellicent, Honedge→Aegislash and ~18 more lines render placeholder icons linking to 404s

Only evolution_details[0] is ever rendered, so 44 of 484 links hide their modern method behind a retired one (Leafeon shows 'at Eterna Forest', never the Leaf Stone), and branching families are laid out in one flat row that reads as linear

The detail route re-fetches over the network data the app already ships: AbilityCard issues useAbility per ability and MoveDetailModal issues useMoveDetail, while ABILITIES (373 entries with effect text) and MOVES (937 with type/power/acc/pp/effect) sit resident and unread

`npm run generate:data` — the single documented pipeline command — throws on `b.firmness.name` for four null-firmness berries before writing types.json and generations.json, both hard imports in data.ts, so a clean regeneration leaves the build unable to compile; the shipped data required three undocumented patch scripts with fetch/pool logic triplicated across them
Every detail page fires GET /pokemon-species/0 → 404 because PokemonDetail.tsx:37 passes `speciesId ?? 0` through a guard testing `!= null` — the app's one measured console error, self-inflicted

Accessibility stops at aria-labels: four modals with no role=dialog, aria-modal, focus trap, scroll lock or Escape; move details reachable only by mouse via bare `<tr onClick>`; no aria-pressed on any filter toggle; no prefers-reduced-motion despite two infinite animations and a 5s auto-advancing text rotation with no pause
No sorting on any surface but the browse page, so a 937-row moves dex and a 2,223-item grid can only be filtered; items have no detail view at all and berries have no search
The 326 form rows carry l:false/m:false and inherit their base species' generation, so Legendary+Forms silently omits every Mega and legendary form, and Megas file under Gen 1-3
A copy-pasted GitHub Octocat path ships as the Psychic type icon in production, rendered inside every Psychic badge app-wide
assessment.standout: The build-time data pipeline: a retrying, concurrency-pooled fetcher that emits seven key-minified indexes covering the entire PokeAPI surface, verified correct at full scale, so browse, search, eight-key sort, faceting, the 18×18 type matrix, compare and team analysis all run with zero network — the shame being that the detail route then goes back over the wire for data already sitting in the bundle, and the command that regenerates it all crashes two files short.
